context: Daichi teaches Sho a simple fishing technique by the river.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: しょう、釣りの技術、教えるで。
lines.en: Sho, I'm going to teach you how to fish.
lines.style: Warm Kansai lilt on the opening. Bright, genuine enthusiasm — this matters to him. Teaching voice, patient and inviting. The regional cadence natural, never forced.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん、習いたい。お魚、取りたい。
lines.en: Yeah, I want to learn. I want to catch a fish.
lines.style: Small, soft voice — six years old and hoping. Real warmth underneath. Quiet sincerity without performance. The gentle lift of genuine interest at the end.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.en: Slowly and quietly — that's what you do. You wait.
lines.style: Kansai warmth and patience woven together. Teaching tone, unhurried. Gentle hand-over-hand quality to the instruction. The wisdom of someone who loves this and wants to share it.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Okay — I'll be quiet and still.
lines.style: Small voice, serious now. Concentrating. The earnest commitment of a child who wants to do this right. Soft and focused, not rushing.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 一緒に、釣り、楽しもうな。
lines.en: Come on — let's enjoy fishing together.
lines.style: Kansai closing warmth, bright and tender. The regional swing on the last word. Inviting him in — this is about being together, not just the catch. Real affection underneath.
